column1: # boru Language Specification: Float special values (inf / -inf / nan)
# boru exposes the IEEE-754 special values as lowercase reserved literals,
# following the true / false / none convention: `inf`, `-inf`, `nan`.
# They are parser-emitted Floats and render back to the same tokens, so
#   * cmp / tcmp / sort use a TOTAL order — the IEEE totalOrder (§5.10)
#     greatest; the Float -0.0 strictly before every positive zero).
#     This is what the collection words need (a non-total comparator
#     silently corrupts sort — the bug this fixed).
#   * lt / lte / gt / gte use IEEE §5.11 — any comparison involving
#     NaN is *unordered* (false), and ±0 compare EQUAL. eq is false
#     for NaN, true for ±0 pairs; neq is the negation.

column3: specials survive in a list, render canonically

column1: # ───────── signed zeros: totalOrder in cmp/tcmp/sort, IEEE ±0 equality in the relationals ─────────
# NUR013: IEEE totalOrder (§5.10) places -0 strictly before +0, and the
# total order now honours it. Only the Float -0.0 slots as -0; Integer 0
# and the Big zeros (0n0 / 0d0 — including any negative-zero decimal
# spelling, since big.Rat has no signed zero) slot as +0, keeping the
# order transitive across the 0 / 0d0 / -0.0 triangle. The relational
# words keep IEEE §5.11 (-0 == +0): lt/gt false, lte/gte true. eq/deq
# stay true — so the total order now DISTINGUISHES a pair eq equates,
# the exact inverse of the NaN asymmetry (nan cmp nan = 0, nan eq nan
# = false). Both asymmetries are the recorded two-regime split.

column3: cross-leaf relational: Integer 0 vs -0.0 stays equal
